outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Memory Bottleneck in Large-Scale Model Tuning
outline.description: This introductory chapter establishes the fundamental challenge addressed by the paper: the prohibitive cost of fine-tuning massive Language Models (LLMs). It contrasts traditional 16-bit full-parameter fine-tuning with emerging quantization techniques used primarily for inference, highlighting the gap in training capabilities.
subtopics: Understanding Parameter Scale: Why 65B+ models are currently inaccessible to individual researchers
The Mechanics of Traditional Fine-Tuning: Activations, Gradients, and Optimizer States
Why Existing Quantization Methods Fail During Backpropagation
Defining the Goal: Achieving High-Fidelity Fine-Tuning within Consumer Hardware Constraints

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Foundational Concepts – From Quantization to LoRA
outline.description: Before diving into QLoRA's specifics, this chapter reviews the necessary background theories. It covers how block-wise quantization manages numerical stability and explores Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) as a mechanism for parameter-efficient updates, setting the stage for combining them.
subtopics: Principles of Block-Wise K-Bit Quantization and Rescaling Strategies
Deep Dive into Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA): Factorized Projections and Trainability
Analyzing Memory Footprints: Comparing Activation Gradients versus Adapter Parameters

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Architecture of QLoRA – Three Pillars of Efficiency
outline.description: This central technical chapter dissects the three core innovations that constitute QLoRA. Readers will understand how NormalFloat handles distributional assumptions, how Double Quantization compresses metadata, and how Paged Optimizers utilize virtual memory management to handle overflow.
subtopics: (a) 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4): Information-Theoretic Optimal Quantization for Gaussian Distributions
(b) Double Quantization: Compressing Quantization Constants Without Precision Loss
(c) Paged Optimizers leveraging NVIDIA Unified Memory for Spill-over Management
(d) The QLoRA Forward Pass and Backward Propagation Workflow
